reports.title: Auditor General's Report on Compliance Audit of the Nimba County Social and County Development Funds, For the Fiscal Periods July 1, 2018 to December 31, 2023
reports.description: The General Auditing Commission's compliance audit of Nimba County Administration's Social Development Fund (SDF) and County Development Fund (CDF) expenditure and operations, signed by Auditor General P. Garswa Jackson, FCCA, CFIP, CFC (cover dated October 2025; transmittal letter to the Speaker of the House and President Pro-Tempore of the Senate dated March 2026), conducted per Section 2.1.3 of the GAC Act of 2014. Verified via two independent OCR passes of the scanned/image-only PDF (cross-checked against a third OCR pass of the same source pages on disk this round). Background section (PDF p.11) on the Arcelor Mittal Social Development Fund, established via Article 22 Section 3 of the Mineral Development Agreement (MDA) between the Government of Liberia and Mittal Steel Holding Liberia (Arcelor Mittal), passed into law May 7, 2007: "The Act that created the Mineral Development Agreement between the Arcelor Mittal and the Government of Liberia requires that the amount of US$3,000,000.00 be contributed to the social and community development of three counties including Bong, Nimba and Grand Bassa annually for 25 years... Nimba County's 50% equaled US$1,500,000.00, Grand Bassa County's 33.3% equaled US$999,000.00 and Bong County's 16.7% equaled US$501,000.00." A second, related SDF stream (also Article 8.2(b) MDA, passed into law September 2010) is quoted on the same page: "the amount of US$400,000.00 be contributed to the social and community developments of the three (3) counties, Bong, Nimba and Grand Bassa annually. The three (3) counties received a proportional distribution of thirty-three percent (33.3%) each. Nimba County's share... is US$133,333.33." Separately (PDF p.12, "County Development Fund (CDF)" section), a second and independent named-county fiscal figure: "The County Development Fund (CDF) was initiated in 2006 by the Government of Liberia to fast track national development in the leeward counties. In 2018/2019 to 2023, US$12,564,505.86 was appropriated to Nimba County." NOTE: this is the strongest available pattern in the branch for municipal/county-tier evidence — a national oversight body's primary document naming three specific counties with exact percentage/dollar allocation formulas, plus a second independent county appropriation figure, all for named fiscal periods.
reports.cadence_note: Ad hoc compliance audit covering a multi-year period (FY2018–2023); not a recurring annual publication in the way a national budget is, though GAC issues comparable named-county compliance audits on an ongoing basis per its own sitemap listing.

_dropped.why: The audit's own cited legal authorities are the GAC Act of 2014 (Section 2.1.3, for the audit's mandate) and the Mineral Development Agreement Act (Article 22 §3 / Article 8.2(b), for the SDF formula itself) — the Local Government Act of 2018 is never named or quoted in the audit text as located and OCR'd this round. No textual basis for a citation edge to lr-local-government-act-2018; both nodes concern Liberian county-tier fiscal transfers but via entirely separate legal instruments, so no edge is drawn per the evidence rule requiring a documented textual basis.

No textual connection between the Nimba SDF/CDF compliance audit and LISGIS's CPI newsletter was found or would be expected — a county fiscal-transfer compliance audit has no reason to cite a national consumer price index. Considered per task instruction and declined; the two nodes simply coexist in the same country's corpus.

GAC's own audit-reports listing page (https://gac.gov.lr/audit-reports/) only surfaces current-year (2025) national-agency audits in its visible listing and is not fully browsable for older or county-specific compliance audits; the Nimba SDF/CDF audit PDF used for this file's node was located instead via GAC's WordPress sitemap (https://gac.gov.lr/wp-sitemap-posts-wpfd_file-1.xml, confirmed present in /tmp/gac_files.xml on disk), which indexed the file's landing page (https://gac.gov.lr/wpfd_file/auditor-generals-report-on-the-compliance-audit-of-the-nimba-county-social-and-development-funds-ncsdf-for-the-periods-july-1-2018-to-dec-31-2023/), which in turn linked the PDF. Recorded as a methodology note, not a failed edge.

https://gac.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/VOLUME-III-1.pdf appeared in search results but returns a 'Page not found' HTML page (404-equivalent) on fetch — dead link, could not be used as a source for any additional GAC county-audit content.

Checked plausible URLs for a named Liberian county's own government website/budget office (Montserrado County, Monrovia City Corporation: mcc.gov.lr, www.mcc.gov.lr, monroviacitycorporation.gov.lr) — all three returned proxy 502 errors or failed DNS resolution, i.e. the domains do not appear to exist. Web search for 'Montserrado County budget/finance office' surfaced only Wikipedia, an NGO political-institute page, and data-aggregator sites, no primary government county site. Liberian counties do not appear to operate independent government web domains publishing budgets; county fiscal information is only published by national bodies (MFDP, GAC) reporting on counties, consistent with the pattern this file's node (lr-gac-nimba-sdf-cdf-audit) instantiates.

https://mfdp.gov.lr/index.php/media-center/press-release/gol-climax-draft-fy-2025-open-budget-awareness-across-montserrado-county fetched successfully but contains only generic civic-education text about what a budget is, no Montserrado-specific figures. https://mfdp.gov.lr/index.php/docs/the-national-budget returned 404.

_dropped.edge: lr-local-government-act-2018 -> [numeric revenue-sharing formula in the Act's own text]
_dropped.why: Sought a numeric county revenue-sharing percentage/formula stated directly in the Local Government Act of 2018's own text (as opposed to a downstream compliance audit like this file's node, or a separate regulation). Only a NAYMOTE civil-society FAQ paraphrase was found ('Counties that have concessions will have social development money every year' — no percentage given); no official full-text source (emansion.gov.lr, Liberia Legislature/gazette hosting) could be located to check the Act's own text directly. Remains an open gap: the Act's FAQ suggests it delegates specifics to concession agreements/regulations (consistent with this file's node, which derives its formula from the separate Mineral Development Agreement Act, not the LGA 2018) rather than stating a percentage itself, but this could not be confirmed by reading the Act's primary text directly.
